brief: Goldman's weekly positioning note reports a hedge fund and CTA de-grossing: beta-adjusted fundamental long/short gross leverage fell 8.3pts to 214.2% (a one-year low) and beta-adjusted net leverage fell 8.8pts to 48.2% (a five-year low); this week's shorting activity was the largest since April 2025; CTAs turned short the S&P 500 and Nasdaq and are modeled as sellers over the next week and month, in any market scenario on the one-week horizon. VIX traded above 35 and Friday was the 4th-largest options-volume session ever, putting Goldman's Vol Panic Index at 9.8/10; AAII read Bearish and CNN's Fear & Greed Index fell to 10/100 (Extreme Fear). Against this, mutual funds and ETFs took in nearly $170bn since Q4 started, buybacks ran at 2.2x their 2025 pace, and retail flows stayed on the bid. Goldman's bottom line: the clean-up has been uneven across investor cohorts, there is little consensus, and the next catalyst is unclear. It frames two open questions before investors re-risk: whether 2026 is a 2018 analog, and whether the Fed will pivot in response to tighter financial conditions.
